candidates.title: IMLU & KELIN High Court case on the right to emergency medical treatment: minor Diana Chepn'geno died after delayed treatment and referral
candidates.snippet: IMLU (@IMLU_org) and @KELINKenya litigated a High Court case over the death of a minor, Diana Chepn'geno, who died following delayed treatment and referral. They argue denial of emergency treatment violates the rights to life, dignity, the highest attainable standard of health, and freedom from cruel, inhuman and degrading treatment, and that Article 43(2) of the Constitution guarantees no one shall be denied emergency treatment. The case summary is published; the matter is now before the Court of Appeal.

candidates.title: Kenyan landmark medical-negligence ruling: cervix removed without consent during a 2006 hysterectomy caused a vesico-vaginal fistula; Ksh 157M awarded
candidates.snippet: Reported by @wambuijoan2024: a Kenyan court delivered a landmark ruling in a nearly two-decade medical-negligence case. Naila Qureshi sued Dr Raffique Parker and two others over a 2006 hysterectomy, saying the doctor removed her cervix without her consent and botched the operation, causing a vesico-vaginal fistula that cost her her job and livelihood; her husband joined citing loss of conjugal life. Justice Alexander Muasya Muteti found the 1st and 3rd defendants grossly negligent and faulted the hospital for letting a doctor disbarred in Uganda practise, awarding about Ksh 157,207,524 in damages — one of the largest medical-negligence payouts ordered by a Kenyan court.
candidates.review_note: SENSITIVE: names an identifiable victim (Naila Qureshi) and describes her private reproductive-health injury.
